1. The response should define what a Sighting card is and its role when playing Twisted Cryptids. For example, Sighting cards are revealed to award/penalize Myth and trigger effects that may move Humans.
2. The response should name the four different sighting card types, namely: Decoys, Hoaxes, Silhouettes, and Real Deals.
3. The response should state the requirements for when sighting cards can be revealed: for example, during the dusk phase of each round, during an encounter at a site in the wilderness, when a player has at least 1 hiding spot at the encounter site.
4. The response should explain how sighting cards are scored once revealed. For example, by gaining or losing myth that depends on the distribution of human types present at the site of the encounter, as specified on the sighting card.
5. The response should explain the following gameplay sequence in order, which happens when a sighting is going to be revealed: 1. reveal the top face down sighting card in the corresponding stack; 2. apply myth gain/loss shown on the card; 3. resolve the sighting’s listed effect; 4. set the revealed sighting face up next to the player; 5. take your hiding spot token from the site of the encounter and place it on its corresponding stack (or if that sighting reveal emptied the stack, return the hiding spot token to the box for the rest of the game); 6. the next player who has a hiding spot at the site of the encounter reveals their sighting.
6. The response should state that players can look at their own sighting cards at any time, but other player's sightings remain hidden until revealed.
7. The response should state that a player can gain 7 Myth from any of their real deal sighting cards that have not been revealed by the end of the game (after 5 rounds).
8. The response should explain how the four different sighting card types work. For example,
1. Decoys: Are objects arranged to look just like you! Use them to trick Hunters and earn Myth.
2. Hoaxes: Enlist the help of woodland creatures to devise Hoaxes and throw Humans off your trail. Reveal Hoaxes to Hikers to increase your Myth.
3. Silhouettes: These shadowy outlines get Researchers excited, earning you Myth with each Encounter. 
4. Real Deals: Real Deal sightings are really you! Expose yourself attacking, sleeping, or engaged in your favorite activity to the right Humans and get rewarded with Myth for your bravery. But beware, you could lose a lot of Myth if the wrong Humans are at the Site of the Encounter.
9. The response should state that each player has nine sighting cards in Twisted Cryptids.
10. The response should state that at the start of the game each player forms 3 stacks of sighting cards that correspond to each player's 3 hiding spot tokens they placed on the board.
11. The response should explain how the encounter site is chosen. For example, it is the site with the most humans and at least one Hiding Spot; if multiple sites have the same amount of humans, then the First Player chooses at which of those sites the encounter occurs.
12. The response should state that each stack contains exactly 3 sighting cards.
13. The response should explain why sighting card order matters in a stack. For example, because unrevealed Real Deal sightings are worth +7 myth at the end of the game.
14. The response should explain how to ‘partially resolve’ a sighting card’s effect if it can’t be fully resolved. For example, if a card states to move three hikers on a site when there are only two - partially resolve that effect to the extent you are able.
